_rule: From /mnt/share/ai/a310-review-models-20261113/round4/rubric.md (written before any answer was seen): 2 = acceptable verdict AND key fact AND nothing invented; 1 = verdict acceptable but key missing/vague, OR key right but verdict off by one step; 0 = wrong verdict by two steps, missed the trap, or an invented fact / wrong causality. key_phrases: regex list, at least ONE must match what+next. forbidden_phrases: any match = 0. forbidden_verdicts: verdict that misses the trap = 0 regardless of steps (only where the rubric calls it out explicitly). cap1_phrases: a wrong-but-not-fatal framing that caps the score at 1. key_required: a missing key fact forces 0 instead of 1 (rubric words it as 0).

h1_dl_404._why: Rubric: key = download failed, HTTP 404/dead link, 0 B; trap: the exit-143 note is for a Stop but this is status 3, so 'ignore' = 0.

h2_router_boot._why: Key = router had just rebooted (Booting Linux / uptime ~48 s), WAN back in seconds; a WAN-outage/cable act is the trap (act is also two steps off = 0).

h3_scrutiny_array._why: Key = Unraid's array/services were stopped, so Scrutiny was unreachable. Blaming Proxmox/CIFS config without the array stop is 1 at most: the key phrase then cannot match.

h4_oom_lxc._why: Key = pi-pocket.service (LXC 116) hit its 6 GiB cgroup limit and restarted itself; 'host out of memory' is wrong causality = 0.

h5_smart_pending._why: Key = disk2/sdc pending sectors rising 0-2-5-8 with a read error = failing disk; back up / plan replacement; ignore = 0 (two steps from act).

h6_jellyfin_cancel._why: Key = Ryan cancelled the library scan; the probe errors come from the cancellation. act = 0 (two steps); claiming file corruption invents a fact.

h7_ext4._why: Key = ext4 corruption on dm-7 = LXC 113's disk (memos); fsck/restore needed. Calling it a hardware failure = 1 at most, so cap1 fires but verdict stays valid.

h8_ssh_flood._why: Key = ~412 failed root/admin logins in an hour from LAN device 192.168.0.157: find that device. ignore = 0, vague (no device/no count) = 1.

h9_gravity_lock._why: Key = lock during the weekly gravity update, resolved seconds later. act = 0 (two steps).

h10_clock._why: Key = clock off by ~3601 s (~1 h), stepped; WireGuard handshakes affected; check RTC/NTP/timezone. ignore = 0 (two steps).

h11_cert._why: Key = cert expires in ~47 h and renewal is rate-limited (429, 5 certs/168 h), so it may lapse; watch without urgency = 1, which the generic one-step rule already gives (watch = verdict off by one).

h12_wifi_flap._why: Key = 183 drops/day, DFS radar on channel 52 forcing switches: move off DFS. The trap is following the 'brief flaps' known-cause note to ignore = 0 (explicit).

h13_watchdog_ok._why: Key = watchdog restarted homelab-dashboard and it recovered (200 OK 30 s later). act = 0 (two steps).

h14_mc_oom._why: Key = the Minecraft container's java hit its docker memory limit (~7 GB RSS), exit 137, restarting; 'host out of memory / hardware' = 0.

h15_dl_stop_plus._why: Key = the download stop is harmless (exit 143 = user stop) BUT nvme0 I/O timeouts / controller reset right after: check the NVMe. Rubric: ignore (missing the NVMe) = 0 and mentioning only the download = 0, so the NVMe key is required (key_required).
